top_strength: Handled the baby grand piano disqualification early, honestly and without losing the sale — he named the limit, explained the gun-safe/pool-table equivalent, and volunteered that specialist movers for it are normal, which kept the customer's trust and led straight into a booking. The 'no hidden fees' pitch was also unusually complete (no credit card fees, no taxes, no travel fees, no material costs).
coaching_note: He booked the move without ever asking where it is going. No origin or destination address, no stairs, no walk distance, no confirmed move date — then quoted 6-7 hours and $2,940 on a 2800 sqft house of marble-top antiques and gave an 8:30 AM Friday start the customer never agreed to. That is exactly the pattern behind our 52% estimate accuracy: the quote has no address, floor, or access data underneath it. Non-negotiable next call — addresses and zips, stairs at both ends, walk/parking, and a confirmed date before any number leaves his mouth. Second priority: with antique marble tops and large antique mirrors on the truck, No Worries Damage Coverage was the single easiest close-strengthener on this call and he never said the words.
phone_presence_notes: Easygoing and likable in spots ('too easy, fantastic,' the joke about the washer/dryer), but transactional overall — he misheard her twice, used her name once, and let a disclosed divorce pass without a single word of acknowledgment.
